structure.title: Demolition and a foothold
structure.text: The first two meditations suspend familiar beliefs and search for what remains certain during that suspension.

structure.title: Reconstructing knowledge
structure.text: The remaining meditations examine God, error, essence, and the relation between mind and body. Each claim must support later steps.

people.name: The thinking self
people.text: Encountered in the act of doubting.

context.title: An exercise in sequence
context.text: Descartes asks readers to inhabit stages of doubt and recovery. Reading the conclusions alone hides what they are supposed to overcome.
context.takeaway: Track what is available at each stage.

context.title: Doubt is methodological
context.text: Imagining deception is a way to test certainty, not automatically a report that Descartes believes a deceiver exists.
context.takeaway: Separate a test possibility from an assertion.

notice.text: Notice apparent returns of discarded assumptions.
notice.why: They reveal where the reconstruction needs justification.
It distinguishes sensory change from judgments about identity.

opening: Descartes sits down to discard every belief that could be false. His senses have deceived him; dreams have felt real; perhaps even his reasoning is being manipulated. Once the demolition begins, ordinary assurances offer little help. These six meditations follow an attempt to find something that survives doubt and then rebuild a world from it. The excitement lies in how much has to be risked for certainty, and how carefully each apparently secure step needs inspecting before the next can bear weight.
